rationale.conceptual: The paper presents its own derived closed-form expression for absorption, combining matrix elements of the Morse potential with Boltzmann factors and a Debye-frequency integration. Correct implementation requires understanding of quantum mechanical matrix elements, combinatorial factors, energy-conservation constraints, and high-temperature approximations. It is not an off-the-shelf algorithm; several interacting components and detailed physics must be accurately translated into code.
rationale.execution: The workflow consists of a single numerical evaluation step, producing one CSV file. No external tooling, no multi-stage pipeline, no data fetching or environment dependencies beyond standard Python libraries.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a custom double-summation formula (Eq. 40) derived in this specific paper for multiphonon absorption using Morse potentials and a Debye spectrum. The method involves non-trivial physics (matrix elements, partition functions, energy-conservation conditions) and careful numerical handling of binomial coefficients via log-gamma. Execution is trivial: a single Python script computes the sum and writes a small CSV; no pipeline, no external data, no tooling. Resources are negligible (no GPU, no datasets).
